meta.title: Vol, Exhaustion & Trade-Management Research Inventory
meta.scope: Gold, NQ, EURUSD (plus the 63-track ladder-v2 rollout where relevant); CFD (OANDA M1) and futures (CME via NT8)
method: Read-only. No code was changed and no backtest was re-run to build this inventory.

Four parallel reads of the research register (plans/RESEARCH_REGISTER.md) and every results file it points to, grouped as: forecasting models; level behaviour & exhaustion; VWAP & futures vs CFD; trade management & sessions.
A study counts as evidence only if a results file exists. Code alone is classed "implemented but not evaluated".
Every number on this page is quoted verbatim from its source file (the "Proof" line). The build script fails if a quote cannot be found, so a number here cannot drift from the file it cites.

clarification.title: "Exhaustion VALIDATED" does not mean "reversal"
clarification.text: In ladder-v2, exhaustion is the calibrated probability that price travels on to the next rung, given the time of day. It is validated (59/63 tracks). Every test of the lines as reversal points, fades or follows is NULL. Both statements are true at once: the forecast tells you how far price is likely to go, not which way.

proof.text: separately. This is a probability of further travel ("is the move used up?"), not a reversal or a trade.

proof.text: - **The OH/OL imbalance is the holdout's direction.** These weeks fell more than they rose. It affects both calcs

**Part A.** Each line type (HL, OH, OL) gets the σ model that forecasts it best, judged on that line's whole distribution and chosen on earlier years only. Does that ladder beat the one-model ladder, where one σ is chosen for all lines? Our mixing study (`ladder-mix-2020s`) chose per percentile, per regime and per 30-cell map, all on the tail-hit score. Three choices, one per line type, each on that line's own who…

rows.area: Best OC forecast, and its KPI
rows.work: OC was never part of model selection, only of the 12-rung guard
rows.result: No OC-specific model exists. ladder-per-line Part B1 will choose OC on mean pinball loss, the same accuracy score as the other lines. That rewards predicting the close well, which is exactly what Jordan warned against for an exhaustion use. Part B2 (OC p50 as a take-profit) is the only purpose-based measure planned.
rows.remaining: What KPI fits OC's job? It can still be amended before ladder-per-line scores.

proof.text: **Part B1.** Does an OC model chosen on OC's own score beat the one-model ladder's OC lines? The race score never included OC. As context, how far is the OC p50 line from the OH/OL p50 line? Under a random walk the running maximum and |close − open| share one distribution, so they should be close.
- **PRIMARY, per quantity q:** mean pinball loss over the five τ, in % of the open. It is a proper score for the whole distribution, rewarding calibration and sharpness together.

**Part B2.** As Jordan suggests, use the chosen OC line as a take-profit. Fade the first touch of the per-line OH/OL p75 line and take profit at the same-side OC p50 line. Does that make money after costs, and does the OC level beat take-profits placed at other distances?

rows.result: Stops in σ units are validated: their hit rate is steadier month to month than fixed-width stops (+3.86pp), and the stop-odds model beats σ alone (Brier skill +4.73%). There is no market-wide noise threshold. 0 of 1,008 stop × target cells is profitable.

proof.text: - **`-steady` VALIDATED.** A σ stop's hit rate is steadier month to month than a fixed-width stop's: Δ SD +3.86pp [+1.85, +5.78]. Every check holds. The prereg expected this cell to be underpowered. It passed anyway.

conflicts.d: "Blends did not beat the best model" holds for the pilots, but blends win 6 rollout tracks. The 80% rule is refuted, not just untested. "Exhaustion validated" means calibration, not reversal.
Older pinball and QLIKE studies favour it; ladder-v2's regime calibration says it over-corrects (slopes 1.13–1.4).
The extension atlas says a grinding approach makes a return to VWAP less likely; the fixed-sigma atlas says a grind reverts and a spike continues. They use different units and outcomes.
